content:
maria: @oncall urgent escalation from AcmeApp — they report a p99 latency regression on our hosted /v1/generate route in us-west-2. They started seeing issues around 09:20 UTC. Their dashboard shows p95 > 3s, p99 ~ 8-12s, and frontend timeouts after 10s. Request IDs they sent: req_0a12, req_0a13. They said retries started getting 429s. Raising to P1.

alex: digging in traces and proxy metrics now. I can see a correlated spike in request_queue_length and long wait times in proxy -> backend-pool-6. Traces show requests waiting in queue for multiple seconds before worker pickup.

sre-bot: :rotating_light: alert fired: latency_p99 > 6s on route "/v1/generate" (us-west-2) — ratio 0.13 at 2026-03-14T09:22:14Z

jamie: quick Qs — are they pinned to a single model version? Any recent rollout in that pool? Also, any kernel or quantization changes last 24h?

maria: customer is pinned to gpt-small-v2@2026-03-14-rc2 (we confirmed). No internal rollout at 09:00 that touched that pool, but there was an autoscaler tweak earlier this morning for unrelated tenants.

alex: initial hypothesis: transient overload of backend-pool-6 due to a combination of longer sequence lengths from this customer and smaller-than-expected worker count after autoscaler adjustments. Also seeing a bursty pattern consistent with retry storms from upstream clients.

alex: immediate mitigations I'm recommending and starting now:
1) Route AcmeApp traffic to fallback compatible model gpt-small-v1 in us-west-2 (same tokenizer, lower perf profile) to reduce per-request latency.
2) Enable per-account soft rate limit (50rps) + circuit breaker (open after 5s average queue wait) for their org to stop retries hammering pool.
3) Temporarily increase worker_count for backend-pool-6 and trigger dedicated-burst capacity for 15 minutes.
4) Send a config to enable prefix KV caching for their account to reduce repeated prefix compute.

jamie: I'll open the incident ticket and run the routing change.

inc-bot: INC-2026-0453 created: "AcmeApp p99 regression — routing + rate limit mitigation" assigned to eng-sre.

jamie: applying routing change now via control plane API — command:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/internal/routes/override -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"org_id":"acme-001","from_model":"gpt-small-v2@2026-03-14-rc2","to_model":"gpt-small-v1@2026-02-28-stable","reason":"latency mitigation"}'
```

jamie: enabling temporary rate limit + circuit breaker for org acme-001:

```json
{"org_id":"acme-001","rate_limit":50,"circuit_breaker_ms":5000}
```

support-ops: messaged AcmeApp, asked for permission to switch model and told them we expect reduced latency at cost of mild quality regression. They accepted and asked for rollback if they see issues.

alex: applied worker_count bump and enabled burst. Also toggled KV prefix caching for acme-001. Changes applied at 09:45 UTC. Monitoring now — initial numbers look promising (per-tenant metrics):
- before: p95 ~ 3.4s, p99 ~ 9.6s
- after (09:51): p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.2s
No reported timeouts from customer yet.

maria: good work. We should also add short-term SLO guardrails to prevent recurrence. Proposed SLO guardrails: 
- per-route p99 alerting with dynamic baselines (notify at +40% over rolling 7d p99)
- auto-fallback threshold: if route p99 > 2s for >5m AND queue_depth > X then route to fallback model/region
- per-org soft rate limit defaults (200rps) with hard cap (500rps) tunable by support
- circuit breaker policy: open if avg_queue_wait > 2s for 1m

alex: I've added a short playbook entry to the runbook and created a dashboard: /internal/runbooks/latency-fallback (link). Playbook includes steps: detect -> validate -> apply fallback -> throttle -> scale -> notify customer -> postmortem.

jamie: action items assigned: 
- alex: follow up with infra about autoscaler policy that reduced workers this morning; validate we have spare capacity for bursts.
- jamie: update runbook with exact API calls and add a checklist for support when contacting customers.
- support-ops: draft customer postmortem and send update by EOD.

support-ops: customer confirmed improved latency and no immediate quality blockers. They asked for a short post-incident summary.

alex: leaving the temporary changes in place for 2 hours and monitoring. Will schedule a controlled rollback to original model only after 24h stable metrics or after a scheduled canary with reduced QPS.

maria: follow-ups for longer term: add model-compatibility labels so fallback routing is automatic when available; instrument per-account sequence length histograms for better autoscaler signals; add canary traffic rules for any autoscaler or pool changes.

jamie: created follow-up ticket OPS-2026-112 for runbook updates and AUTOSCALE-2026-77 for policy changes.

maria: thanks @alex @jamie @support-ops :thumbsup: — please update INC-2026-0453 with any new telemetry. I'll close the Slack thread when the customer confirms stable at +2h.
